setup: A new store owner has not previously operated an online shop and is signed in to the GAMMA-J web store onboarding area.
action: The store owner starts the guided setup for a new online store.
expected_observation: The system presents a straightforward web store setup flow with store details, products, customers, and order management features suitable for a first-time online merchant.

setup: The first release of GAMMA-J is being used for a small retail shop that sells standard products only.
action: The store owner attempts to configure a specialized catalog item, subscription plan, marketplace listing, multi-warehouse inventory rule, or deep ERP/accounting integration.
expected_observation: The system indicates that these advanced capabilities are not available in the first release and limits the store to basic small-shop retail operations.

setup: A store owner is signed in with administrative privileges on a newly created store.
action: The store owner opens the setup, product, customer, and business settings areas from the admin interface.
expected_observation: The system allows access to store-wide setup, product management, customer oversight, and business settings in the back office.

setup: A sales staff member is signed in with staff-level access to the store back office.
action: The sales staff member opens product maintenance, customer account assistance, order review, and routine store update screens.
expected_observation: The system allows the staff member to maintain products, assist with customer accounts, review orders, and perform routine store updates.

setup: A customer visits the public storefront on a desktop or mobile browser and is not signed in to any back-office role.
action: The customer browses the product catalog, adds an item to the cart, and proceeds to checkout.
expected_observation: The system lets the customer browse products, manage the shopping cart, and place an order through the storefront.

setup: A customer is signed in to the public storefront and attempts to navigate to an administrative page by using a back-office URL or menu path.
action: The customer selects a store management or admin function from the attempted back-office entry point.
expected_observation: The system blocks access to back-office functions and does not expose administrative controls to the customer.

setup: A store operator is signed in with permission to configure a new storefront, and no storefront has been published yet.
action: The store operator completes the storefront setup form with store name, branding, and basic shop details and saves the configuration.
expected_observation: The system creates the storefront and makes the public shop presence available with the entered store identity and basic configuration.

setup: A staff user with product management permission is in the back office product area.
action: The staff user creates a new product and later edits an existing product record.
expected_observation: The system saves the new product and applies the updates to the existing product record in the product catalog.

setup: The product catalog is open for editing by an authorized staff user.
action: The staff user enters a standard retail product with a product name, description, price, and available quantity.
expected_observation: The system accepts the product data and displays the product in the catalog with its name, description, price, and stock quantity.

setup: An authorized staff user is viewing an existing product in the product management screen.
action: The staff user adds a new product and updates the price and available quantity of an existing product, then saves both changes.
expected_observation: The system stores the added product and persists the updated product details without losing the existing catalog entries.

setup: A staff user with customer account permissions is signed in to the back office, and a customer record already exists.
action: The staff user opens the customer record and updates the customer contact details or account status.
expected_observation: The system saves the customer account changes and shows the revised customer information in the account record.

setup: The storefront contains products organized into simple categories such as clothing, accessories, and home goods.
action: A customer browses a category and applies a basic filter such as price range or category refinement.
expected_observation: The system displays the matching products only, using clear categories and simple filters that narrow the visible catalog.

setup: A customer is browsing the storefront with an empty shopping cart.
action: The customer adds a product to the cart, changes the item quantity, and removes the item from the cart.
expected_observation: The system updates the cart contents and quantities immediately, showing the current items and totals after each cart change.

setup: A customer has one or more items in the shopping cart and is ready to complete a purchase.
action: The customer proceeds to checkout and submits the order through the store.
expected_observation: The system places the order, confirms the purchase, and shows an order completion message or order reference to the customer.

setup: The store supports product catalog onboarding with file import enabled, and an authorized staff user is preparing new product data for the catalog.
action: The staff user imports a valid product file to load multiple products into the catalog.
expected_observation: The system accepts the file import and creates or updates the product catalog entries from the uploaded file. If file import is not enabled, the system only offers manual product entry and does not present an import option.

setup: Before launch, the site is in a pre-publication state and a staff user has access to the product administration area.
action: The staff user imports the initial product catalog file into the web store's catalog management area.
expected_observation: The system loads the products into the catalog and displays the imported product listings as ready for staff review, without exposing them to customers on the live storefront.

setup: The initial product catalog has been loaded and the site is still not marked live for customers.
action: A staff member opens the loaded catalog and reviews product entries for titles, images, pricing, and availability status.
expected_observation: The system shows the product listings in a review view where staff can verify correctness of images, prices, and availability before approval.

setup: A staff member has completed catalog review and no blocking issues remain.
action: The staff member marks the product catalog as ready for customers.
expected_observation: The catalog status changes to ready for customers and the storefront is allowed to present the approved products to shoppers.

setup: The storefront contains multiple products organized into categories, and customer browsing is enabled.
action: A customer browses a category, then applies a price filter and a search term to narrow the product list.
expected_observation: The system returns only products matching the selected category, search text, and filter criteria, and updates the visible results accordingly.

setup: A registered customer account exists and the login page and password reset flow are available.
action: The customer signs in with valid credentials, then initiates a password reset request for the same account.
expected_observation: The system authenticates the customer securely and sends a password reset path through the supported reset flow without exposing the current password.

setup: The storefront is receiving normal customer traffic and fraud monitoring is active.
action: A customer submits an obviously suspicious activity pattern, such as repeated failed login attempts from the same account in a short period.
expected_observation: The system flags the activity for attention or review instead of trying to automatically resolve every aspect of the suspicious behavior.

setup: Checkout is configured to use an external trusted payment provider.
action: A customer enters payment details during checkout and completes the payment step.
expected_observation: The system sends payment processing to the trusted provider and does not display or store full sensitive card details in the web store.

setup: A customer is placing an order for physical goods through the checkout flow.
action: The customer proceeds through checkout and is prompted to enter shipping and contact information.
expected_observation: The system requests only the personal data needed to fulfill the order and does not require unnecessary personal fields beyond what is needed for fulfillment.

setup: The checkout and fraud screening services are active for incoming orders.
action: A customer submits a transaction that matches a high-risk pattern, such as mismatched billing indicators or unusual order behavior.
expected_observation: The system blocks the transaction or routes it for review instead of completing it immediately.

setup: An authorized administrator is signed in and administrative actions are enabled.
action: The administrator changes a product price and then updates the stock quantity for the same product.
expected_observation: The system records both administrative changes in the audit log.

setup: An administrator has edited a customer account status and the audit log is available for review.
action: A staff auditor opens the audit entry for that administrative change.
expected_observation: The log shows who made the change, when it happened, what changed, and the before-and-after values for the important fields involved.

setup: A product price, product stock level, order status, and customer account status are each changed by authorized staff actions.
action: A reviewer opens the relevant audit records for those changes.
expected_observation: Each audit record includes the before-and-after values for the important field that changed, such as the old and new price, stock quantity, order status, or customer account status.

setup: The storefront is under a sudden increase in browsing traffic and non-urgent actions such as wishlist updates and background recommendations are available.
action: Many customers browse the site at the same time while some non-urgent actions are triggered during the peak load.
expected_observation: The site remains responsive for browsing, and non-urgent actions are slowed down or queued rather than causing the store to fail outright.

setup: A customer has items in the cart and has already started checkout when one backend service becomes temporarily unavailable.
action: The customer continues browsing and attempts to proceed with the existing cart and checkout progress while the partial outage is in effect.
expected_observation: The cart contents and existing order progress are preserved, and the customer can continue from the last safe point once the unavailable service is restored.

setup: A partial service outage is active, affecting only one part of the storefront such as recommendations or order tracking.
action: A customer visits the site and attempts to use the affected and unaffected areas.
expected_observation: The system clearly states which feature is unavailable and which parts of the store remain usable, instead of showing a generic failure message.

setup: The web store is operating normally with customer browsing, cart, and checkout services online, while some back-office admin functions such as catalog bulk editing are temporarily degraded due to maintenance.
action: A customer searches for a product, adds it to the cart, and proceeds to checkout during the admin service degradation.
expected_observation: The storefront browsing, cart, and checkout functions remain available, and the customer can complete the purchase without being blocked by the reduced admin features.

setup: An administrator is creating or editing a product record in the catalog management screen.
action: The administrator uploads one main product image and a small set of additional product images for the same product.
expected_observation: The product saves successfully with one designated main image and the allowed additional images attached to the product.

setup: An administrator is on the product image upload form for a new or existing product.
action: The administrator uploads a JPG image for the main product image and a PNG image as an additional image.
expected_observation: The system accepts both files as valid image uploads and displays them as attached product images without format errors.

setup: An administrator is editing a product and has initiated an image upload for that product.
action: The administrator attempts to upload a corrupted image file or an unsupported file masquerading as an image.
expected_observation: The system rejects the upload with a clear error message, does not save a broken product record, and keeps the user on the product form so the upload can be tried again.

setup: A product exists in the catalog without any image files attached.
action: A customer opens the product detail page.
expected_observation: The product remains visible and purchasable according to its other status rules, and the page shows a default placeholder image instead of a broken or empty image area.

setup: A product is listed in the catalog with an active status and marked available for sale.
action: A customer adds the product to the cart and starts the checkout flow.
expected_observation: The product can be added to the cart and purchased normally because it is active and available for sale.

setup: Stock control is enabled for the store, and a product has a defined stock quantity.
action: A customer attempts to purchase the product when its stock is zero or otherwise invalid for sale.
expected_observation: The system prevents the purchase of that product and indicates that the item cannot be bought until valid stock is available.

setup: A customer has already placed an order for a product at an earlier price, and the product price is then updated in the catalog.
action: A second customer adds the same product to a new cart after the price update, while the first order remains recorded in the order history.
expected_observation: The new cart and any new order use the updated product price, while the previously placed order keeps the original price and does not change unexpectedly.

setup: A product is configured as out of stock or not yet available for sale.
action: A customer views the product page and attempts to add the item to the cart or proceed to checkout.
expected_observation: The product is shown as unavailable, and checkout for that product is blocked with a clear indication that it cannot currently be purchased.

setup: A product is configured with minimum and maximum purchase quantities, for example a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 5 units per order.
action: A customer tries to add fewer than the minimum quantity or more than the maximum quantity of that product to the cart.
expected_observation: The system refuses the invalid quantity and informs the customer of the allowed minimum and maximum quantity limits for the product.

setup: The store has an order-level limit configured, such as a maximum total quantity or a maximum order value.
action: A customer builds a cart that exceeds the configured order limit and attempts to continue to checkout.
expected_observation: The system blocks checkout for the over-limit cart and shows that the order must be adjusted to comply with the configured total quantity or value limit.

setup: A customer has a cart that is above either a product quantity limit or an order value limit before checkout.
action: The customer opens the cart and attempts to proceed to checkout without correcting the over-limit items.
expected_observation: The system flags the cart before checkout and explicitly tells the customer which product quantity or order total must be reduced to continue.

setup: The deployment includes support for importing an initial product catalog from a legacy file, and an administrator has a valid import file prepared.
action: The administrator uploads the catalog import file through the catalog import function.
expected_observation: The system processes the file import and creates or updates the initial product catalog entries from the file.

setup: A product migration is in progress and the source file contains records that do not match the target data structure cleanly.
action: The migration is run against the source file containing the ambiguous or mismatched records.
expected_observation: The system reports the unmapped records for manual review instead of filling in values by guesswork.

setup: A legacy product record is being imported or migrated and essential information such as name, category, or price is missing.
action: The migration processes the incomplete legacy product record.
expected_observation: The system either skips the incomplete record or marks it as needing attention, and the product is not treated as a clean, ready-for-sale catalog item until corrected.

setup: A store admin or designated catalog owner is signed in to GAMMA-J Web Store, and there is a legacy product record flagged for manual review because it is incomplete or inconsistent.
action: The admin opens the product review queue and selects the legacy product record for review.
expected_observation: The system opens the record in a manual review view and allows the admin or catalog owner to assess, edit, and annotate the product record.

setup: A legacy product record has been created for manual review and contains known gaps such as a missing category and inconsistent pricing information.
action: The reviewer updates the review status and adds notes describing the missing category and the pricing inconsistency.
expected_observation: The review record is saved with a status of pending or in review, and the notes clearly list the missing or inconsistent fields.

setup: A product record is currently under manual review because required fields are incomplete and an approval has not yet been granted.
action: A customer browses the storefront or attempts to access the product directly, and a catalog user tries to publish the record.
expected_observation: The product does not appear in customer-facing search or category listings, and the system blocks publishing until the required fields are corrected and approval is completed.

setup: The storefront contains multiple categories and products with descriptive content, tags, and filterable attributes such as brand, price, and size.
action: A shopper browses a category and also performs a broad search using a general term such as a product type or use case.
expected_observation: The system presents category navigation and search results with clear product descriptions and relevant filters that help the shopper narrow to the correct items.

setup: A customer is signed in and has an active account that may be suspended or deleted on request.
action: The customer submits a request to suspend the account or delete the account through the account management area.
expected_observation: The system accepts the request and starts the account suspension or deletion handling process.

setup: A customer submits a standard suspension request that has no blocking exception or additional manual dependency.
action: The customer confirms the account suspension request.
expected_observation: The account becomes suspended immediately and the customer is informed that access is no longer active.

setup: A customer submits an account deletion request for an account that has one or more active orders, unresolved payment issues, legal retention requirements, return cases, refund cases, unresolved support cases, or order history needed for service or accounting.
action: The customer confirms deletion of the account.
expected_observation: The system does not delete the account immediately and shows that deletion is delayed because of the active dependency or retention reason.

setup: A customer deletion request cannot be completed automatically because an exception is detected, such as conflicting account data or a policy edge case.
action: The deletion request is submitted and the automated handling fails to determine a safe outcome.
expected_observation: The request is routed to an admin for exception handling, and the account remains pending until the admin resolves it.

setup: A customer account request contains ambiguous or conflicting information that prevents the system from confidently deciding whether suspension or deletion is safe.
action: The customer submits the account request for automated processing.
expected_observation: The system places the request in an admin review queue before any suspension or deletion is carried out.

setup: A customer record has been created or updated with missing required fields and inconsistent profile data such as mismatched contact or address information.
action: The record is submitted for activation or normal processing.
expected_observation: The customer record remains in review until all required fields are completed and the inconsistent data is corrected.

setup: A customer record is incomplete in a way that could disrupt ordering, shipping, or account access, such as a missing shipping address or invalid login-related data.
action: The customer or staff member attempts to make the record available for normal use.
expected_observation: The record stays hidden from the customer and is not exposed for normal account use until the issue is resolved.

setup: A customer record has been corrected so that all required data matches the expected rules, and it is waiting for review approval.
action: An admin or authorized staff member approves the customer record.
expected_observation: The customer record becomes live and available for normal use only after approval is granted.

setup: A shopper has added items to the cart and the quantity for at least one item exceeds that shopper's customer-specific purchase limit.
action: The shopper proceeds toward checkout without reducing the excessive quantity.
expected_observation: The cart clearly flags the limit violation and checkout is blocked until the quantity is lowered or the item is removed.

setup: A customer has successfully completed checkout for an order that may include shipping charges and applicable taxes or fees.
action: The order is confirmed and the confirmation page is displayed.
expected_observation: The customer sees the order number, purchased items, quantities, totals, any applicable taxes or fees, shipping details, and the payment status.

setup: A customer has just completed checkout and provided a valid email address on the order.
action: The order is placed successfully.
expected_observation: An order confirmation email is sent to the customer containing the completed order details.

setup: A customer is browsing a product detail page in the GAMMA-J web store. The product is configured to remain visible in the catalog, but its price is either missing, marked invalid, or the inventory is unavailable while stock control is enabled.
action: The customer opens the product page and attempts to purchase the item from the add-to-cart or buy-now controls.
expected_observation: The product remains visible on the page, but the purchase controls are disabled or unavailable. The system does not allow the item to be added to the cart and indicates that the product cannot be purchased because the price is unavailable, invalid, or stock is exhausted.

setup: A customer is viewing a product that is currently not purchasable because its price is missing or invalid, or because stock control shows no available inventory.
action: The customer tries to add the product to the cart and proceeds toward checkout.
expected_observation: The system blocks the add-to-cart and checkout actions. A clear on-screen message explains why the product cannot be purchased, such as missing price, invalid price, or unavailable inventory.

setup: The customer is on the shipping address form during checkout and the cart contains at least one item ready for delivery.
action: The customer enters an address with an obvious missing or invalid component, such as no street address, no postal code, or an invalid country or state value, and submits the form.
expected_observation: The system rejects the address and highlights the missing or invalid fields. A validation message explains that the shipping address must be completed with valid address components before checkout can continue.

setup: The customer has entered a valid shipping address and is on the delivery options step of checkout.
action: The customer requests available delivery methods for the entered location.
expected_observation: The system shows delivery options that are appropriate for the customer's location. Available methods may differ by region, and only methods supported for that address are presented.

setup: The customer has entered a shipping address for which no delivery method is available.
action: The customer continues from the shipping step into delivery selection or checkout review.
expected_observation: Checkout stops at the delivery step. The system informs the customer that no delivery method is available for the address and tells them to change the address or contact support.

setup: The customer is on the payment step with a populated order summary showing the final amount due.
action: The customer selects a payment method and reviews the displayed amount before confirming payment.
expected_observation: The system allows the customer to choose a payment method and shows the amount to be charged before final submission. Payment is not finalized until the customer confirms after reviewing the amount.

setup: The customer has submitted payment for an order from the payment step.
action: The payment gateway response returns either success or failure.
expected_observation: The system immediately displays a clear success message when payment succeeds or a clear failure message when payment fails, without leaving the customer waiting without feedback.

setup: The customer has submitted payment and the transaction is declined or otherwise fails.
action: The system receives the failed payment result.
expected_observation: The system explains what the customer can do next, such as retrying payment or choosing a different method, and keeps the customer on a recoverable checkout state rather than forcing them to restart the entire order.

setup: The customer has completed payment submission and the payment is approved in full.
action: The successful payment confirmation is received by the store.
expected_observation: The order moves immediately to confirmation, and the customer is shown that the purchase is complete, with a success confirmation visible on screen.

setup: A payment attempt has failed during checkout and the order has not been completed.
action: The customer chooses the recovery options presented after the failure, such as trying payment again, selecting a different payment method, or returning to review the order.
expected_observation: The system allows the customer to retry payment, switch to another payment method, or return to the order review step without losing the entire checkout session.

setup: A payment attempt has partially completed, such as an authorization or capture that does not cover the full order amount.
action: The system receives a partial payment result for the order.
expected_observation: The order does not confirm as complete. It remains unresolved until the remaining amount is handled, and the system prevents premature completion of the purchase.

setup: A new order has been created from checkout and the system has not yet completed payment and availability verification.
action: The order is submitted into the post-checkout processing flow.
expected_observation: The order is placed in a pending state while payment and stock availability are checked.

setup: An order is pending review, full payment has been accepted, and all ordered items have been confirmed available for shipping.
action: The system completes the payment and availability checks successfully.
expected_observation: The order is allowed to move into fulfillment, with the order no longer held in pending review and ready for downstream processing.

setup: An order is pending and at least one blocking condition exists, such as an out-of-stock item, an unresolved payment, or an open staff review.
action: The system evaluates the order for progression into warehouse fulfillment.
expected_observation: The order remains waiting and does not move to picking and packing. The blocking condition prevents fulfillment until it is resolved.

setup: A submitted order exhibits one or more review triggers, such as suspicious payment activity, mismatched customer and shipping details, unusual order size, or a policy exception.
action: The order processing workflow flags the order for staff attention.
expected_observation: The system places the order into a manual review state and makes it available for staff assessment rather than sending it directly to fulfillment.

setup: A customer order has completed manual review and the reviewer has marked the order as approved.
action: The order review outcome is saved and the customer views the order status in the web store account area or receives the order update notification.
expected_observation: The customer is told that the order is confirmed and moving ahead, and the order status shows that processing will continue.

setup: A customer order has been manually reviewed and the reviewer leaves the order on hold because the review is not yet complete.
action: The latest review result is recorded and the customer checks the order status message.
expected_observation: The customer is told that the order is still under review and that no action may be needed yet.

setup: A customer order has been manually reviewed and the reviewer has marked the order as rejected.
action: The rejection result is saved and the customer opens the order details or receives the decision notification.
expected_observation: The customer is told that the order cannot be completed, and the message includes appropriate next steps such as trying again or contacting support when relevant.

setup: A manual review issue has been raised, but staff do not yet have enough information to make a quick decision.
action: The reviewer attempts to finalize the order decision before the issue is fully verified.
expected_observation: The order remains on hold and is not approved or rejected until the issue can be verified.

setup: A manual review identifies missing information that must be provided by the customer before the order can proceed.
action: Staff send the review outcome back to the customer for action from the order review screen.
expected_observation: The order is returned to the customer with clear instructions describing what information is missing and what the customer must do next.

setup: A manual review issue is confirmed to be internal, and staff still need to investigate before making a final decision.
action: The reviewer records the issue without approving or rejecting the order.
expected_observation: The order stays on hold and remains unavailable for completion until staff later approve or reject it.

setup: An order is currently in a real operational state such as unpaid, on hold, canceled, or ready for fulfillment.
action: A staff member attempts to change the order status through the web interface to a status that does not match the current order state.
expected_observation: The web interface allows only the status changes that are valid for that order's real state and prevents any mismatched transition.

setup: A staff member is viewing an order status transition screen with an attempted invalid transition available, such as moving a canceled order back to normal processing without a reopen step.
action: The staff member submits the invalid status change.
expected_observation: The web interface blocks the change and shows a plain-language explanation of why the transition is not allowed.

setup: An order exists in an unpaid state and has not yet been paid by the customer.
action: A staff member attempts to move the unpaid order into fulfillment.
expected_observation: The system prevents the move into fulfillment and keeps the order out of the fulfillment stage.

setup: An order has been canceled and is no longer in normal processing.
action: A staff member attempts to return the canceled order to normal processing without using the deliberate reopen action.
expected_observation: The system blocks the transition back to normal processing and only permits reopening when the deliberate reopen action is used.

setup: A low-risk, frequently changed business rule is available for administration through configuration or business settings.
action: An administrator updates the setting through the web interface without deploying a new application release.
expected_observation: The change is accepted through configuration or business settings and takes effect without requiring code changes.

setup: A change request affects the core checkout flow, security behavior, or introduces a major new capability.
action: A business administrator attempts to apply the change only through configuration or business settings.
expected_observation: The system indicates that the change requires code updates and a new release rather than a simple configuration change.

setup: An administrator is on the web interface import screen and has a customer, product, or order data file in a common format such as CSV or Excel.
action: The administrator uploads the file for import.
expected_observation: The web interface accepts the import file through the browser and begins processing the uploaded data.

setup: A data file has been uploaded for import and contains one or more rows to be added or updated.
action: The administrator submits the import for processing.
expected_observation: Every imported row is checked before becoming active, and no row goes live unless it passes validation.

setup: An import file contains a row that conflicts with an existing product record, such as a duplicate SKU or incompatible product identifier.
action: The administrator runs the import for that file.
expected_observation: The conflicting row is stopped or flagged for review, and the existing product data is not silently overwritten.

setup: A product feed or inventory sync job is available for the GAMMA-J Web Store, and the operator has access to a validation view that compares incoming data against the live catalog.
action: The operator runs a future automatic sync file that contains changes to an existing product's price and inventory, where one of the incoming values does not match the allowed source rules or current catalog constraints.
expected_observation: The system does not publish the mismatched change to the live store, shows a clear mismatch report identifying the affected product and fields, and leaves the existing live product data unchanged until the discrepancy is validated.

setup: An administrator starts an import of customer or product records from a file that contains several valid rows followed by one or more malformed rows; the import mode is configured for either partial import with reporting or full rollback for critical data sets.
action: The administrator launches the import and the process fails partway through after processing some rows successfully.
expected_observation: If the dataset is non-critical, the system imports only the clean rows and presents a report listing each failed row with the reason it was rejected; if the dataset is marked critical, the system stops the entire import and none of the records from that file are applied.

setup: A new store operator is signed in through the web interface with permissions to manage orders but has only basic order-processing access.
action: The operator opens an order and changes its status from 'New' to a supported processing state such as 'Packed' or 'Shipped' using the order status controls on the web page.
expected_observation: The updated status is saved and displayed immediately in the order view, and the order history shows the status transition without requiring a back-office tool or manual database update.

setup: A customer is signed into their web account and has an order that is currently marked as 'Preparing for delivery' in the order history.
action: The customer opens the order details page for that order.
expected_observation: The current preparation-for-delivery status is visible on the page, along with the order reference and tracking-related status information available to the customer.

setup: A customer has items in the shopping cart, and at least one cart item has become unavailable since it was added, such as being removed from catalog availability or no longer offered for sale.
action: The customer proceeds from the cart to checkout without first updating the unavailable item.
expected_observation: The checkout flow is interrupted with a prompt identifying the unavailable item and requiring the customer to remove it or replace it with an available alternative before the order can be submitted.

setup: A product exists in the store catalog with its listing visible to shoppers, but its price is missing or invalid, or inventory is unavailable while stock control is active.
action: A shopper opens the product detail page and attempts to add the product to the cart or buy it directly.
expected_observation: The product remains visible in the catalog, but purchase actions are blocked and the interface indicates that the item cannot be bought until the price or inventory issue is resolved.

setup: Stock control is enabled for the store, and a product is configured with insufficient or invalid stock for the requested quantity.
action: A shopper attempts to purchase that product through checkout.
expected_observation: The system rejects the purchase because valid stock is required under stock control, and the checkout shows an inventory-related message instead of completing the order.

setup: A product is marked as out of stock or not yet available for sale in the storefront.
action: A shopper tries to proceed to checkout with that product in the cart.
expected_observation: Checkout is prevented for that product, and the customer is informed that the item is unavailable or not yet available for purchase.

setup: A product is displayed on the storefront with an unavailable status visible to shoppers.
action: A shopper clicks Add to Cart and then attempts to continue to checkout for that same product.
expected_observation: Both add-to-cart and checkout actions are blocked for the unavailable product, and the shopper sees a clear availability message rather than being allowed to complete the order.

setup: A customer enters payment information during checkout, and the payment process is configured to use a compliant payment service.
action: The customer submits card details to place an order.
expected_observation: The store completes payment processing without retaining the full card number, CVV, or equivalent full card data in the order record or customer profile.

setup: A customer record contains sensitive information such as internal notes, fraud indicators, or protected support details, and a staff user is signed in with a role lacking permission to view restricted data.
action: The staff user opens the customer or order record.
expected_observation: Only authorized staff with a legitimate need to know can view the sensitive data; the unauthorized staff member cannot access the restricted fields.

setup: An order has normal contact details, order details, sensitive notes, refund references, and fraud-related flags, and a staff member is assigned either a sales role or a support/admin role with case assignment applied as required.
action: The staff member opens the assigned order record.
expected_observation: Sales staff can see the normal contact and order details but not the sensitive notes, refund references, or fraud flags; support or admin staff assigned to the case can see the sensitive fields, while unassigned staff cannot.

setup: A customer places an order that requires shipping information, and the checkout form collects address and contact details.
action: The customer completes checkout and the order is saved.
expected_observation: Only the minimum contact and shipping information needed to fulfill the order is retained, and unnecessary personal fields are not stored with the order.

setup: Store data includes both normal order information and sensitive customer information such as protected notes or fraud-related data, and staff access roles are configured.
action: Different staff users attempt to open the same customer or order record from the web interface.
expected_observation: Sensitive data is exposed only under stricter access controls than normal store data, so users with ordinary store access can see standard details but are denied access to the protected data unless they have the elevated permission required.

setup: A customer submits an account deletion request while the account has active orders, unresolved support cases, or other retention-triggering records such as payment issues, legal recordkeeping, return cases, or refund cases.
action: The customer confirms the deletion request.
expected_observation: The deletion does not proceed immediately, and the system explains that the account cannot be removed while the listed active obligations or required history still exist.

setup: A customer account request is submitted in the web store with one of the following conditions already attached to the applicant profile: an unresolved dispute, a suspicious activity flag, or a conflict with an open order or refund.
action: A store administrator opens the account request queue and reviews the submitted request.
expected_observation: The request is not auto-approved; it is marked for admin approval review and the administrator can see the reason category that triggered the hold.

setup: A customer account request arrives with incomplete or ambiguous risk signals, so the system cannot confidently determine whether it is safe to proceed.
action: The account request is submitted for processing.
expected_observation: The request is routed to admin review instead of being approved automatically, and the review queue shows it as requiring manual decision.

setup: The store catalog contains one product marked inactive or not available for sale, and another product marked active and available for sale.
action: A customer attempts to add each product to the cart and proceed toward checkout.
expected_observation: Only the active, available product can be purchased; the inactive or unavailable product cannot be added for checkout and the customer is informed that it is not currently for sale.

setup: A customer has already placed an order, and later the merchant updates the price of the purchased product before the customer creates a new cart.
action: The customer views the existing order and then starts a new cart containing the same product after the price change.
expected_observation: The already placed order retains the original price, while the new cart uses the updated price.

setup: A customer has added items to a cart whose total quantity or total value exceeds the store's checkout limits.
action: The customer clicks the checkout button without reducing the cart contents.
expected_observation: Checkout does not continue, and the customer sees a message indicating the cart exceeds allowed limits and must be adjusted before purchase can proceed.

setup: A customer enters a shipping address that is structurally valid, but the address conflicts with the selected shipping method or carrier rule, such as a service area restriction.
action: The customer attempts to continue checkout with that shipping method selected.
expected_observation: The system displays a warning that the address conflicts with the chosen delivery option and allows the customer to select a different shipping method or use a different address.

setup: The checkout form is open and the shipping address fields are available for entry.
action: The customer submits an address missing one or more obvious required elements, such as street, city, postal code, or country.
expected_observation: The address is rejected during validation, the missing fields are highlighted or listed, and the customer cannot proceed until the address is completed.

setup: A customer-facing order or account request enters manual review due to a fraud or security concern.
action: The system generates the review message shown to the customer.
expected_observation: The message uses neutral language such as needing review or verification and does not reveal internal fraud scores, security rules, detection methods, or investigation details.

setup: An administrator performs a sensitive action, such as viewing a restricted record or approving a manual review item, and audit logging is enabled for operational records.
action: The administrator completes the action from the back office interface.
expected_observation: An audit entry is created showing who performed the action, what record was viewed or changed, and the reason or context when available.

setup: An admin is creating or editing a product record and selects an image file that fails upload or cannot be processed as a valid product image.
action: The admin submits the product form with the broken image upload attached.
expected_observation: The product record is not saved, the form returns an image upload error, and the admin must replace or remove the invalid image before saving.

setup: A customer has a valid cart and proceeds to payment from the checkout page.
action: The customer submits payment for the order.
expected_observation: The payment request is sent through the trusted payment provider, and the checkout shows the resulting approved or declined payment response from that provider.

setup: A customer has completed an order using an email address that can receive messages.
action: The order is confirmed by the store.
expected_observation: An order confirmation email is sent to the customer with the order details and confirmation information.

setup: A store administrator opens the product import page and has a valid CSV or Excel file containing product data prepared for upload.
action: The administrator uploads the file through the web interface and starts the import.
expected_observation: The system accepts the CSV or Excel file, imports the product data, and reports the number of products processed, added, or updated.

setup: The store has existing product data in a legacy system and the migration source is available for import.
action: An administrator initiates the product migration from the legacy source.
expected_observation: The system brings the legacy product data into the web store and presents a migration result summary showing the records transferred or any records that require attention.

setup: A new store owner signs in to the admin area for the first time and has basic access to common store setup tasks.
action: The owner configures a simple store setting, such as adding a product, updating a price, or reviewing an order, without using advanced technical tools.
expected_observation: The interface allows the task to be completed through clear forms and labels with minimal training, indicating the system is straightforward for non-technical users to operate.

setup: The web store is open with active product listings, a working shopping cart, and an available checkout flow during normal business hours.
action: A customer browses products, adds an item to the cart, updates the quantity, and proceeds through checkout to place an order.
expected_observation: The product pages, cart, and checkout continue to work without crashing, data loss, or repeated reload failures, and the order can be completed successfully.

setup: The web store is being accessed by a normal baseline number of shoppers on supported devices and browsers.
action: Several additional customers begin browsing category pages, searching products, and opening product details at the same time.
expected_observation: Pages continue to load within an acceptable time, navigation remains usable, and browsing interactions do not freeze, time out excessively, or return service unavailable errors.

setup: The web store is operating normally and a sudden traffic spike begins from many customers browsing at once.
action: During the spike, multiple customers submit non-urgent actions such as wish-list updates, product reviews, and account preference changes.
expected_observation: The store does not fail outright; non-urgent actions are delayed, queued, or shown as temporarily pending, while core browsing and shopping remain available or degrade gracefully with clear feedback.

setup: An administrator is on the product import and data review page with a file selected for upload.
action: The administrator submits an import file containing missing required fields, invalid values, or duplicated product identifiers.
expected_observation: The system highlights the validation problems in plain language, identifies the affected rows or fields, and clearly indicates whether the import was rejected or which records need correction before review can continue.

setup: A customer has an item in the cart, and the order status or payment state is currently in a condition that blocks the next action.
action: The customer attempts an invalid status transition or tries to complete a blocked purchase, such as checking out an unavailable item or retrying a completed order.
expected_observation: The system prevents the invalid action and displays a clear, plain-language message explaining why the transition or purchase is blocked, without exposing technical error codes.

setup: The web store is available and the same customer account can be accessed from multiple supported browsers.
action: A user opens the store in Chrome, Safari, Edge, and Firefox and performs key tasks such as browsing products, adding to cart, and starting checkout.
expected_observation: The store interface renders correctly and the core shopping flow works in each of the supported browsers without broken layouts or blocked functionality.

setup: The web store is accessible from a desktop computer, a mobile phone, and a tablet with standard network connectivity.
action: A customer opens the store on each device type and completes common actions such as searching, viewing product details, and using the cart.
expected_observation: The site adapts to the screen size and input method, remains usable on desktop, mobile, phone, and tablet, and core actions can be completed without horizontal overflow or unusable controls.

setup: A partial service outage affects a non-critical backend component, while the sales area and catalog are still partially available.
action: A customer browses products and attempts to place an order, while staff continue using essential sales functions such as viewing orders or processing available checkout steps.
expected_observation: Important sales functions remain available where possible, affected features show a graceful limitation or fallback, and the system does not completely shut down when only part of the service is unavailable.

setup: A customer has entered valid checkout details and is on the payment submission step.
action: The customer submits payment for the order.
expected_observation: Immediately after submission, the system displays a clear success message if the payment is accepted or a clear failure message if it is not, without leaving the customer uncertain about the result.

setup: A payment attempt is made using a card that is invalid, declined by the bank, or interrupted by a system issue.
action: The customer submits the payment and the transaction fails.
expected_observation: The failure message explains whether the problem is a card issue, a declined transaction, or a system issue, using plain language that helps the customer understand the next step.

setup: A customer has successfully completed checkout and the order has been accepted by the store.
action: The checkout process finishes and the confirmation page or confirmation notice is shown.
expected_observation: The customer immediately sees confirmation information such as order number, purchased items, total amount, and next-step guidance, with no need to refresh or search for the result.

setup: A product is unavailable, or the customer's cart contains an item that cannot be purchased due to stock, policy, or checkout restrictions.
action: The customer attempts to add the unavailable product to the cart or continue checkout with the blocked cart.
expected_observation: The system stops the action and displays clear messaging that states the product is unavailable or explains why the cart or checkout is blocked, in language suitable for customers.

setup: The live catalog is currently serving customers, and a store operator is preparing an onboarding import that includes new product data.
action: The operator runs an import that changes onboarding data, then uses the rollback option after detecting a problem in the import results.
expected_observation: The live catalog remains unchanged by the faulty onboarding changes, and the operator can safely roll back the import so that only the intended catalog state remains visible to customers.

setup: New onboarding rules have been configured, and existing products are already present in the catalog before the change.
action: The operator loads a new batch of products that should follow the updated onboarding rules while existing catalog items remain in place.
expected_observation: The new batch is processed according to the new rules, while products already stored in the system keep their existing valid data and are not broken or retroactively altered unexpectedly.

setup: A new store operator has a standard web login account and is using a regular browser on a managed or unmanaged workstation with no special software installed.
action: The operator signs in to the web interface and performs basic administrative tasks such as reviewing products, updating simple settings, and checking orders.
expected_observation: The operator can access and use the basic administrative functions directly in the web interface without requiring command-line tools, local installation, or technical setup beyond signing in.

setup: A customer has items in the cart and is on the payment step of checkout with a valid shipping address already entered.
action: The customer submits payment, but the card is declined or only a partial payment amount is authorized.
expected_observation: The order is not confirmed, no order confirmation number is issued, and the checkout remains in a failed or pending payment state with a clear payment failure message.

setup: A seller is creating or editing a product listing and is on the product image upload section.
action: The seller attempts to upload an invalid image file or the image upload process fails before completion.
expected_observation: The product is not saved with a broken or placeholder image record, the image field remains unassigned, and the system shows an upload validation or failure message.

setup: A customer has items in the cart and has entered a shipping address for checkout.
action: The customer proceeds to shipping options and the system evaluates the address but finds no delivery method available for that location.
expected_observation: Checkout stops at the shipping step, no delivery option is presented, and the customer is informed that the selected address cannot be served.

setup: A customer has a cart containing items that exceed one or more business limits, such as quantity, total weight, or item count.
action: The customer tries to continue from the cart to checkout.
expected_observation: The system blocks checkout progression, highlights the cart limit violation, and requires the customer to reduce or correct the cart before checkout can continue.

setup: An order has entered manual review and staff have not yet completed a quick verification decision.
action: The system attempts to process the order while the manual review is still unresolved and no customer follow-up action has been completed.
expected_observation: The order remains on hold, it is not released for fulfillment or completion, and the order status indicates that staff review or customer action is still pending.

setup: An order is in a state other than eligible fulfillment, such as pending payment, on hold, canceled, or awaiting review.
action: A user or system process attempts to transition the order directly into fulfillment.
expected_observation: The transition is blocked, the order state does not change to fulfillment, and the system presents an error or warning stating that the order is not eligible for fulfillment.

setup: The first release is configured with the standard cart and checkout rules only, with no customer-specific limit rule enabled.
action: A customer with no special account restrictions adds products and proceeds through checkout.
expected_observation: Checkout behavior follows the standard shared limits only, and no customer-specific limit message or enforcement is shown.

setup: A customer reaches the payment step where the current first-release flow supports email confirmation as the available payment-related communication channel.
action: The customer completes checkout and awaits payment-related confirmation.
expected_observation: The system provides the supported email-based confirmation flow; no additional payment channel is exposed in the checkout experience unless explicitly configured elsewhere.

setup: A customer is placing an order in the first-release store and reaches the payment authorization step.
action: The customer confirms the order during checkout.
expected_observation: The order proceeds using the release's configured payment timing; the user-facing flow reflects the implemented timing without exposing an alternative capture policy choice.

setup: A customer accesses the web store from a browser that may be considered older or legacy, such as one below the currently supported version range if any is defined.
action: The customer opens the storefront and attempts to browse products and begin checkout.
expected_observation: The system either operates normally within the supported browser set or displays a compatibility notice for unsupported browsers, depending on the release configuration; no unsupported-browser requirement is assumed.

setup: An administrator is preparing to add product data in the first release environment.
action: The administrator looks for a file import option to upload catalog data in bulk.
expected_observation: Only the import capability explicitly supported by the release is available; if no file import feature exists, the UI does not offer one and the administrator is not able to start a file-based import.

setup: A future onboarding or catalog sync process is being evaluated for product data updates.
action: An administrator attempts to perform a bulk update or synchronization using an onboarding method not yet defined for the release.
expected_observation: The system does not present undocumented import or sync behavior, and any unsupported update method is rejected or unavailable until the exact rules are specified.

setup: The store is operating under the first-release configuration with no explicit customer-specific limit policy selected.
action: A customer places items into the cart and proceeds toward checkout as if a personalized limit might apply.
expected_observation: Only the currently defined shared cart and checkout limits are enforced; no customer-specific limit enforcement appears unless that capability has been explicitly enabled.
